learn.hook: From the snows of Kashmir to the waves at Kanniyakumari is over 3,200 km. India's extent explains much of its variety.
points: The mainland of India extends from Kashmir in the north to Kanniyakumari in the south, and from Arunachal Pradesh in the east to Gujarat in the west.
India's territorial limit extends into the sea up to 12 nautical miles (about 21.9 km) from the coast.

Latitudinal extent of the mainland: 8°4'N to 37°6'N. Longitudinal extent: 68°7'E to 97°25'E. Both are roughly about 30 degrees. (The southern boundary of the country reaches 6°45'N in the Bay of Bengal, at Indira Point.)

The north–south extent is about 3,214 km, but the east–west extent is only about 2,933 km. This is because the distance between two lines of longitude decreases towards the poles, whereas the distance between two lines of latitude remains the same everywhere.

example.q: Calculate India's latitudinal extent of the mainland from 8°4'N to 37°6'N.
steps: Degrees: 37 − 8 = 29°; minutes: 6' − 4' = 2'.
Extent = 29°2', i.e., roughly 29 degrees (about 30 degrees).

learn.reallife: The Indian Coast Guard patrols up to 12 nautical miles as India's territorial waters, and further in the Exclusive Economic Zone.

topics.title: The Tropic of Cancer and effects of India's extent

learn.hook: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states. North of it the climate is subtropical; south of it, tropical.
points: The Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) divides India almost into two equal parts. The southern part lies within the tropics, and the northern part lies in the subtropical or warm temperate zone.
Because of this latitudinal extent, day length varies: the difference between day and night is small near Kanniyakumari but much larger in Kashmir, especially in summer and winter.
India's longitudinal extent of nearly 30 degrees causes a time difference of nearly two hours between the easternmost and westernmost parts of the country (4 minutes per degree of longitude).
So the sun rises in Arunachal Pradesh about two hours earlier than in western Gujarat.

example.q: How much earlier does the sun rise at 97°E than at 68°E? (Earth rotates 1° in 4 minutes.)
steps: Difference in longitude = 97 − 68 = 29°.
Time difference = 29 × 4 = 116 minutes.
116 minutes = 1 hour 56 minutes, nearly two hours.
example.answer: About 1 hour 56 minutes, nearly two hours earlier.

learn.reallife: Many in the North-East have long argued for an earlier time zone because sunrise there can be before 5 a.m. in summer, well ahead of office hours based on IST.

learn.hook: Trains in India run on one clock from Dwarka to Dibrugarh. That clock is set by a line passing near Mirzapur.
points: To avoid confusion from different local times, India uses one standard time. The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30'E, passing through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh. Time along it is Indian Standard Time (IST).
IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT): 82.5° × 4 minutes = 330 minutes = 5 h 30 min.
Countries usually choose a standard meridian that is a multiple of 7°30' (half-hour time steps), so their time differs from GMT in clean half-hour units. 82°30' = 11 × 7°30'.
Some countries with vast east–west extent use more than one standard meridian; for example, the USA has seven time zones.
To find local time: each degree of longitude = 4 minutes; places east of a meridian are ahead, places west are behind.

example.q: When it is 12:00 noon IST, what is the local time at 90°E (near Dhubri, Assam)?
steps: Longitude difference = 90° − 82.5° = 7.5°.
Time difference = 7.5 × 4 = 30 minutes.
90°E is east of the Standard Meridian, so local time is ahead.
Local time = 12:00 + 30 min = 12:30 p.m.

learn.reallife: Every Indian Railways timetable, ISRO launch countdown and RBI clearing schedule follows IST, keeping the whole country in sync.

topics.title: Size, coastline and boundaries of India

learn.hook: India is the seventh largest country, yet it packs in the world's highest mountains, a great desert, vast plains, two seas and hundreds of islands.
points: India's area is 3.28 million sq km, about 2.4% of the world's total land area. It is the seventh largest country in the world.

Its size gives it great physical diversity: the Himalaya in the north, the Indian Ocean in the south, a desert in the west and forested hills in the east. Its location in the tropics and subtropics, between the Himalaya and the Indian Ocean, also gives it a monsoon climate, which is classified in detail (including Koeppen's scheme for India) in the chapter on climate.
The mainland coastline is about 6,100 km; including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep, the total coastline is about 7,517 km.

India is bounded by young fold mountains in the north-west, north and north-east. South of about 22°N, the peninsula begins to taper and extends into the Indian Ocean, dividing it into the Arabian Sea on the west and the Bay of Bengal on the east.

example.q: How much of India's total coastline (7,517 km) belongs to its islands, if the mainland coastline is 6,100 km?
steps: Island coastline = 7,517 − 6,100.

learn.reallife: India's long coastline supports major ports such as JNPT (Mumbai), Chennai and Visakhapatnam, and millions of fishing families.

learn.hook: India sits at the head of the Indian Ocean, the only ocean named after a country. Its location connects it to West Asia, Africa, South-east Asia and beyond.
points: India is located in the south-central part of Asia, bordering the Indian Ocean and its two arms, the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal. This maritime location provides links with neighbouring regions by sea and air.
India's central location at the head of the Indian Ocean is strategically important for trade routes between east and west.
Land neighbours: Pakistan and Afghanistan in the north-west; China (Tibet), Nepal and Bhutan in the north; Myanmar and Bangladesh in the east.
Island neighbours: Sri Lanka, separated from India by the Gulf of Mannar and the Palk Strait; and the Maldives, located south of the Lakshadweep Islands.
Map work: mark the latitudinal and longitudinal extent, the Standard Meridian (82°30'E), the Tropic of Cancer, Kanniyakumari, and India's neighbours on an outline map.
